cim: X and xAI escape a payout in South Africa’s media inquiry
kihagyva: P3: 51 pont, tendencia 20%, jóváhagyás után fordul
cim_eredeti: X and xAI escape a payout in South Africa’s media inquiry
szoveg_eredeti:
Elon Musk’s X and xAI have settled with the Competition Commission over the remedies imposed on them by its media and digital platforms market inquiry, agreeing to train South African news publishers rather than fund them.

Both companies had appealed the inquiry’s findings and remedies to the Competition Tribunal. They have now withdrawn those appeals, the commission said on Wednesday. In return, it has amended the remedies imposed on X Corp, which runs the social media platform X, and withdrawn those imposed on xAI, replacing them with a voluntary undertaking.

xAI, the maker of the Grok chatbot, is now known as SpaceX Super Intelligence, after SpaceX acquired it in February.

X was the only platform that did not reach agreement with the commission before the inquiry’s final report in November 2025. The report required it to make all its monetisation programmes available in South Africa, run twice-yearly workshops for publishers and fund digital literacy programmes. The publisher support and literacy programmes were to run for three years.

These commitments are an important step in translating the … final report into practical benefits for South African news publishers.

Under the settlement, X’s commitments run for two years. It will launch a monetisation support programme for publishers within six months, with twice-yearly workshops on its revenue tools. To get access, publishers must attend at least one workshop and meet X’s own “rules and integrity criteria”. X will provide its paid Premium tier for two years where publishers need it to qualify, after which they will have to pay for it. “Revenue calculations remain unchanged,” the commission said, so publishers will earn on the same terms as other X creators.

Workshops will be translated into “up to five” local languages, but only “subject to sufficient demand”. They will also show publishers how to stop their public posts being used to train Grok.

xAI’s undertaking is narrower still. The inquiry had required it to train publishers on how to control the use of their content to train its AI models and inform its answers. Instead, xAI will run twice-yearly training on Grok’s settings and on robots.txt, the file websites use to tell crawlers which pages they may visit, for two years.

Neither company has committed any money to South African media. Google, by contrast, agreed in November 2025 to a support package worth R688-million, including R71-million a year for five years through Google News Showcase. Meta and TikTok agreed to publisher training and support programmes.

The inquiry found that AI chatbots had scraped South African news without agreement or compensation. The xAI undertaking does not compensate publishers for content already used. It shows them how to opt out.

The commitments cover South African print, online, radio and video news organisations that report primarily on current affairs and are members of the Press Council or the Broadcasting Complaints Commission of South Africa.

“These commitments are an important step in translating the MDPMI [media inquiry] final report into practical benefits for South African news publishers,” said James Hodge, the commission’s chief economist, who chaired the inquiry. – (c) 2026 NewsCentral Media
